title: Determination of toxicological relevant arsenic species in urine by hydride generation microwave-induced plasma optical emission spectrometry
author: Pizzorno, Falchi, et al.

steps.title: Collect urine samples
steps.instruction: Collect urine after at least 2 h retention in urine cups; for workplace monitoring collect at the end of a workweek following ACGIH guidelines.

steps.title: Freeze and transport specimens
steps.instruction: Freeze specimens to below –10 °C, store in a portable cooler for transport to the laboratory, and analyse within 15 days using the HG‑MP‑AES procedure.

steps.title: Prepare mixed urine matrix (MFU)
steps.instruction: Combine urine from at least three healthy, non‑exposed volunteers; stir the mixture for 2 min, centrifuge 15 min at 28 000 g, then let stand at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Make calibration and QC solutions
steps.instruction: For each calibration level (0, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200 µg L⁻¹) and QC level (10, 35, 100 µg L⁻¹), pipette 4.00 mL MFU into a 10 mL polypropylene tube, add the calculated volume of 2000 µg L⁻¹ As(V) intermediate standard, then add 2 % l‑cysteine solution to reach a final volume of 8.00 mL. Prepare blanks by mixing 4.00 mL MFU with 4.00 mL aqueous 2 % l‑cysteine solution.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 4.00 mL MFU to a 10 mL tube.
Add appropriate volume of 2000 µg L⁻¹ As(V) standard to obtain the target concentration.
Add 2 % l‑cysteine solution and bring volume to 8.00 mL.
Prepare blanks: 4.00 mL MFU + 4.00 mL 2 % l‑cysteine solution.

steps.title: Prepare study urine samples
steps.instruction: Stir each individual urine sample for 2 min, centrifuge 15 min at 28 000 g, let stand 30 min at room temperature, then add 4.0 mL of the sample to 4.0 mL of 2 % l‑cysteine solution.

substeps.instruction: Mix 4.0 mL urine with 4.0 mL 2 % l‑cysteine solution.

steps.title: Mix and incubate with l‑cysteine
steps.instruction: Invert all tubes (calibrators, QC, blanks, study samples) 8–10 times to mix, then let stand at room temperature for a minimum of 30 min (pre‑reduction incubation; signals remain stable up to at least 90 min).

substeps.instruction: Incubate 30 min at room temperature (minimum; stable up to 90 min).

steps.title: Analyze by HG‑MP‑AES
steps.instruction: Introduce the incubated mixtures into the hydride‑generation microwave‑induced plasma optical emission spectrometer (HG‑MP‑AES) and acquire arsenic emission signals according to the instrument’s standard operating procedure.

description: We propose a simple alternative method using atomic emission spectroscopy with microwave-induced plasma (MP-AES). This technique allows the coupling of a chamber for hydride generation (HG-MP-AES). This atomic technique uses nitrogen -instead of argon- from a generator powered by compressed air to sustain the plasma. Additionally, and of notable importance, the instrument's investment and maintenance costs are significantly lower than those of any other atomic technique, and it operates without the need for flammable gases in the laboratory [9]. The proposed method for quantifying As-U involves urine sample preparation through a pre reduction step with l-cysteine. This method is based on the reaction of arsenic species with l-cysteine in an acidic medium, producing thio-derivatives that generate arsines at similar rates. This allows the accurate quantification of the total amount of the four toxicologically relevant species (iAs + MMA + DMA) [10,11]. Arsenobetaine, which can lead to an overestimation of iAs exposure as explained before, is not quantified since it does not form hydrides [12,13]. Method validation was performed following the recommendations of the Eurachem Guidelines [17]. Some parameters of the Standard Practices for Method Validation in Forensic Toxicology [18], such as stability, were also incorporated since they are useful in laboratory routines, particularly when working with biological samples like urine. The evaluated figures of merit were linearity, limit of detection (LOD), limit of quantification (LOQ), precision, accuracy, stability, and external proficiency testing control samples. Linearity was calculated with eight calibration levels at concentrations of 0, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, and 200 µg L−1. The calibration function was evaluated based on an assay with five replicates of each concentration level.
